english_translation: Sahih International (via HS-023): "Say, 'I do not find within that which was revealed to me [anything] forbidden to one who would eat it unless it be a dead animal or blood spilled out or the flesh of swine - for indeed, it is impure - or it be [that slaughtered in] disobedience, dedicated to other than Allah.'"
notes: The four-item list Ghamidi relies on (TR-14 to TR-18). The qualifier "blood spilled out" matters for the liver and spleen hadith (QS-012). Ghamidi's own Al-Bayan rendering (Shehzad Saleem) was not retrieved; it is needed before this is quoted in the final text.

reference: Whatever is cut from a living animal is carrion (maytah)
collection: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 1480; also Abu Dawud, Ahmad, ad-Darimi
grading: Reported as authentic; al-Tirmidhi: acted upon by the people of knowledge
graded_by: hadeethenc.com entry, as summarised in a search result (HS-022)
english_translation: "Whatever is cut from an animal while it is alive is unlawful carrion."
notes: Main text behind the rule that cells taken from a living animal need slaughter of the donor (Hamdan et al. 2018, HS-006, cite Tirmidhi 1480). Abu Dawud number not confirmed. Grader named only as the encyclopedia; the individual hadith critics were not checked.

reference: Two dead animals and two bloods have been made lawful: fish and locusts, liver and spleen
grading: Weak as a Prophetic report (via Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam); sound as a statement of Ibn Umar

english_translation: "Two kinds of dead meat and two kinds of blood have been made lawful for you. The two kinds of dead meat are fish and locusts, and the two kinds of blood are the liver and spleen."
notes: Source of the sea-animal exemption from slaughter, used by MWP Irsyad 595 (FT-003) for marine cells. Grading from search summaries only.
